q-93048.name: Question 2
q-93048.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt[4]{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $q(x)=2\sqrt[4]{x+3}-2,$ we replace $x$ with $x+3$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
x+3\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & \ge 0 \\ x & \ge -3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=q(x)$ is $x\in [-3,\infty ).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=q(x)$ is shown below.

q-98631.name: Question 3
q-98631.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt[6]{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $s(x)=\sqrt[6]{2x-4}+1,$ we replace $x$ with $2x-4$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
2x-4\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-4 & \ge 0 \\ 2x & \ge 4 \\ x & \ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=s(x)$ is $x\in [2,\infty ).$ 

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=s(x)$ is shown below.
